sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.zh: 埃利亚·卡赞拍过另一部惊悚片，一部名为《危机四伏》的电影。

sentences.en: who found time running out as they looked into the face of mortal peril.

sentences.en: When the police investigate, they find the victim suffered from a deadly infectious disease,

sentences.en: a version of the plague.

sentences.zh: 公共卫生官员认为，凶手可能在

sentences.en: What follows is a race to track down the criminals and halt an epidemic,
sentences.zh: 随之而来的是一场追捕罪犯和阻止疫情爆发的竞赛，

sentences.en: a collision of law enforcement and public health.
sentences.zh: 这是执法部门与公共卫生部门的碰撞。

sentences.en: If the killer is incubating pneumonic plague,

sentences.en: Shortly after that, you'll have the makings of an epidemic.

sentences.en: In the first half of our show, we have a story about chaos and an effort to contain it.
sentences.zh: 在我们节目的前半部分，我们有一个关于混乱以及遏制混乱努力的故事。

sentences.en: It's a story about life imitating art.
sentences.zh: 这是一个生活模仿艺术的故事。

sentences.en: It's a story about disease and panic.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于疾病和恐慌的故事。

sentences.en: But it's also a story about psychology.
sentences.zh: 但这也是一个关于心理学的故事。

sentences.en: To control an epidemic takes more than medical skill.
sentences.zh: 控制一场疫情需要的不仅仅是医疗技能。

sentences.en: It requires an understanding of human behavior and the forces that drive people to act in certain ways.
sentences.zh: 它需要对人类行为以及驱使人们做出特定行为的因素有深刻的理解。

sentences.en: Our story starts in Monrovia, the capital of Liberia.
sentences.zh: 我们的故事从利比里亚首都蒙罗维亚开始。

sentences.en: A deadly crisis was sparking fear.
sentences.zh: 一场致命的危机正在引发恐惧。

sentences.en: News reports were filled with dramatic language and catastrophic warnings.
sentences.zh: 新闻报道中充斥着戏剧性的语言和灾难性的警告。

sentences.en: The Ebola virus is back.
sentences.zh: 埃博拉病毒又回来了。

sentences.en: An Ebola breakout in West Africa is, quote, totally out of control.
sentences.zh: 西非的埃博拉疫情用引号来说，已经完全失控。

sentences.en: A catastrophe is unfolding.
sentences.zh: 一场灾难正在上演。

sentences.en: The world's deadliest outbreak of Ebola.
sentences.zh: 世界上最致命的埃博拉疫情。

sentences.en: Highly infectious, quick to kill, with no vaccine and no cure.
sentences.zh: 高度传染性，致死极快，没有疫苗，也没有特效药。

sentences.en: The Ebola outbreak reached its peak in the fall of 2014.
sentences.zh: 埃博拉疫情在2014年秋天达到顶峰。

sentences.en: By the end of the year, it was subsiding.
sentences.zh: 到年底时，它正在消退。

sentences.en: But then, in early 2015, in a poor part of Monrovia, there was a new outbreak, or cluster.
sentences.zh: 但随后，在2015年初，在蒙罗维亚的一个贫困地区，爆发了新的疫情或聚集性病例。

sentences.en: And it led to the complex case we're focusing on today.
sentences.zh: 它引出了我们今天关注的复杂案例。

sentences.en: I got a call from someone who said,
sentences.zh: 我接到一个人的电话，他说，

sentences.en: if your passport isn't in my office in the next two hours, you won't make your flight to Liberia.
sentences.zh: 如果你的护照在接下来的两个小时内没到我办公室，你就赶不上飞往利比里亚的航班了。

sentences.en: Athalia Christie is an epidemiologist with the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, or CDC.
sentences.zh: 阿塔利亚·克里斯蒂是美国疾病控制与预防中心（即CDC）的一名流行病学家。

sentences.en: She flew to Monrovia to help track and stop the outbreak.
sentences.zh: 她飞往蒙罗维亚帮助追踪和制止疫情。

sentences.en: Lots of CDC officials joined her, like Frank Mahoney.
sentences.zh: 许多疾控中心官员和她一同前往，比如弗兰克·马霍尼。

sentences.en: People were scared.
sentences.zh: 人们很害怕。

sentences.en: It was a crisis.
sentences.zh: 这是一场危机。

sentences.en: You could drive to the city and see people that were being left out on the street,
sentences.zh: 你开车进城，会看到人们被留在街上，

sentences.en: you know, for people to come pick them up.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，等着别人来接他们。

sentences.en: Frank and Athalia told me how the case we're following today started.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克和阿塔利亚向我讲述了我们今天所追踪的案件是如何开始的。

sentences.en: Police in Monrovia discovered a body in a warehouse.
sentences.zh: 蒙罗维亚警方在一个仓库里发现了一具尸体。

sentences.en: A young man, dead, with multiple stab wounds.
sentences.zh: 一个年轻人，死了，身上有多处刺伤。

sentences.en: Police were called in.
sentences.zh: 警察被叫到了现场。

sentences.en: A swab was taken, as mandated by the official policy, that any dead body be swabbed.
sentences.zh: 根据官方政策的要求，采集了拭子，即所有死尸都要进行拭子采样。

sentences.en: So even though the police who arrived there initially thought they were investigating a murder,
sentences.zh: 因此，尽管最初到达那里的警察以为他们在调查谋杀案，

sentences.en: they did follow the procedures and have the body swabbed,
sentences.zh: 但他们确实遵循了程序并对尸体进行了拭子采样，

sentences.en: at which point we were alerted because the test came back positive.
sentences.zh: 就在那时我们得到了警报，因为检测结果呈阳性。

sentences.en: Positive for Ebola.
sentences.zh: 埃博拉病毒检测呈阳性。

sentences.en: Once police identified the youth,
sentences.zh: 一旦警察确认了这名年轻人的身份，

sentences.en: they quickly realized they had a major problem on their hands.
sentences.zh: 他们很快意识到自己手头有一个大麻烦。

sentences.en: It turned out the young man was actually part of a large street gang.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，这个年轻人其实是一个大型街头帮派的成员。

sentences.en: Yeah, it was like a gang.
sentences.zh: 对，就像一个帮派。

sentences.en: One of them, for whatever reason, he got stabbed by other members of the group.
sentences.zh: 其中一个人，不管出于什么原因，他被该团伙的其他成员刺伤了。

sentences.en: As we understand it, there was a knife fight.
sentences.zh: 据我们了解，那里发生了一场持刀斗殴。

sentences.en: And we're not quite sure how it happened, but the friends turned on him.
sentences.zh: 我们不太确定事情是怎么发生的，但朋友们背叛了他。

sentences.en: Just to review, a young man contracts Ebola, he gets in a fight,
sentences.zh: 回顾一下，一个年轻人感染了埃博拉，他卷入了一场斗殴，

sentences.en: and it's stabbed repeatedly by fellow members of his gang.
sentences.zh: 并被他帮派的同伙多次刺伤。

sentences.en: Ebola, remember, is highly contagious.
sentences.zh: 记住，埃博拉具有高度传染性。

sentences.en: Come into contact with an infected person's sweat or blood, and you could fall sick too.
sentences.zh: 接触感染者的汗液或血液，你也可能会生病。

sentences.en: The gang had as many as 35 members.
sentences.zh: 这个帮派有多达35名成员。

sentences.en: Each had connections far and wide across the city.
sentences.zh: 每个人在全市都有广泛的联系。

sentences.en: And just like in that movie, Panic in the Streets,
sentences.zh: 就像那部电影《危机四伏》中一样，

sentences.en: public health officials needed to quickly stop the outbreak from spreading.
sentences.zh: 公共卫生官员需要迅速阻止疫情蔓延。

sentences.en: They needed to try and find every person who could have come into contact with the young man.
sentences.zh: 他们需要设法找到所有可能与这名年轻人有过接触的人。

sentences.en: It's a process called contact tracing.
sentences.zh: 这是一个被称为接触者追踪的过程。

sentences.en: It's exceedingly difficult to do.
sentences.zh: 这做起来极其困难。

sentences.en: If you try to imagine constructing the last three weeks of your life
sentences.zh: 如果你试图想象构建你生命中最后三周的生活，

sentences.en: and determining every single person that you came into contact with,
sentences.zh: 并确定你接触过的每一个人，

sentences.en: whether it was casual contact or a family member who you saw every day,
sentences.zh: 无论是泛泛之交还是你每天都能见到的家庭成员，

sentences.en: it's extraordinarily difficult to do.
sentences.zh: 这做起来异常困难。

sentences.en: So we interview people multiple times,
sentences.zh: 所以我们对人们进行多次采访，

sentences.en: and we also talk to their family members and their friends
sentences.zh: 我们还会与他们的家人和朋友交谈，

sentences.en: to try to determine everyone who might have had any contact with this person
sentences.zh: 试图确定在这个人可能具有传染性的这段时间里，

sentences.en: during the time that they could have been infectious.
sentences.zh: 所有可能与这个人有过任何接触的人。

sentences.en: Ethelia and Frank knew the young man who died had sought medical treatment for his stab wounds.
sentences.zh: 埃塞利亚和弗兰克知道，死去的年轻人曾因刀伤寻求过医疗救助。

sentences.en: Had a health care worker suture the young man's wounds and come into contact with his blood?
sentences.zh: 是否有医护人员缝合了年轻人的伤口并接触了他的血液？

sentences.en: Ethelia visited a lot of clinics trying to track down facilities the young man may have visited.
sentences.zh: 埃塞利亚走访了许多诊所，试图追踪年轻人可能去过的医疗机构。

sentences.en: She paged through logbooks of patient names with no luck.
sentences.zh: 她翻阅患者名字的日志，但没有找到。

sentences.en: Then she got to one clinic.
sentences.zh: 然后她来到了一家诊所。

sentences.en: And I took this big, dusty logbook, and I opened it up,
sentences.zh: 我拿起了这本厚厚、布满灰尘的日志，翻开它，

sentences.en: and literally the page I opened it to, there's maybe 30 names to a page,
sentences.zh: 简直就是我翻开的那一页，一页大概有30个名字，

sentences.en: and I read down them, and there he was at the bottom of the first page.
sentences.zh: 我顺着往下读，他就出现在第一页的最底部。

sentences.en: A health care worker at this clinic had sutured the young man's knife wounds.
sentences.zh: 这家诊所的一名医护人员缝合了这名年轻人的刀伤。

sentences.en: Ethelia knew what she had to do.
sentences.zh: 埃塞利亚知道她必须做什么。

sentences.en: The most difficult part of these investigations come when you need to tell the clinicians
sentences.zh: 这些调查中最困难的部分在于，你需要告诉临床医生

sentences.en: and all of the staff who work in these health care facilities
sentences.zh: 以及这些医疗机构中工作的所有员工，

sentences.en: that someone with Ebola entered the facility.
sentences.zh: 曾有埃博拉感染者进入过该机构。

sentences.en: And I remember how nervous the individual was when I told him that the person he sutured
sentences.zh: 我还记得当我告诉他，他缝合的那个人

sentences.en: had been positive for Ebola at the time.
sentences.zh: 当时埃博拉病毒呈阳性时，那个人有多紧张。

sentences.en: And it's hard to imagine what he was going through.
sentences.zh: 很难想象他当时经历着怎样的心理历程。

sentences.en: Can you recall what you told him and what he said?
sentences.zh: 你还记得你对他说过什么，他又说了什么吗？

sentences.en: We were standing in the hallway, and I told him that there's no easy way to tell anybody this.
sentences.zh: 我们当时站在走廊里，我告诉他，向任何人透露这件事都没有什么轻松的办法。

sentences.en: And so we just told him very matter-of-factly,
sentences.zh: 所以我们只是非常客观地告诉了他，

sentences.en: and that we needed to maintain daily contact and monitoring with him,
sentences.zh: 我们需要与他保持日常接触和监测，

sentences.en: coming in for treatment the moment that you have symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 一旦出现症状就要立即来接受治疗。

sentences.en: And the reason I remember this so clearly is that he didn't do that.
sentences.zh: 我之所以把这记得这么清楚，是因为他根本没有那样做。

sentences.en: He was very reluctant to go to an Ebola treatment unit.
sentences.zh: 他非常不情愿去埃博拉治疗中心。

sentences.en: The health care worker refused to be quarantined.
sentences.zh: 这名医护人员拒绝被隔离。

sentences.en: He insisted he'd followed all safety procedures as he bandaged the young man's wounds.
sentences.zh: 他坚称自己在给年轻人伤口包扎时遵守了所有的安全程序。

sentences.en: He told Athelia he'd get in touch if he started to have any symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 他告诉阿塔利亚，如果他开始出现任何症状，他会联系他们的。

sentences.en: Athelia knew there was a reason the health care worker had refused to come into an Ebola treatment unit.
sentences.zh: 阿塔利亚知道，医护人员拒绝进入埃博拉治疗中心是有原因的。

sentences.en: It had to do with a lack of trust in the system.
sentences.zh: 这与对体制缺乏信任有关。

sentences.en: In fact, the more Athelia and Frank saw,
sentences.zh: 事实上，阿塔利亚和弗兰克看到的越多，

sentences.en: the more they realized that Ebola wasn't the only enemy they were fighting in Monrovia.
sentences.zh: 他们就越意识到埃博拉并不是他们在蒙罗维亚与之战斗的唯一敌人。

sentences.en: They were dealing with an epidemic of mistruSt.
sentences.zh: 他们正在应对一场不信任的疫情。

sentences.en: After a long history of civil war and corruption,
sentences.zh: 经历了长期的内战和腐败之后，

sentences.en: a lot of people in Liberia simply didn't trust the government or international organizations.
sentences.zh: 利比里亚的许多人根本不信任政府或国际组织。

sentences.en: When Ebola broke out, the government's first response was to try and control it using coercion,
sentences.zh: 当埃博拉爆发时，政府的第一反应是试图用强硬手段来控制它，

sentences.en: cordoning off sections of towns.
sentences.zh: 用警戒线封锁城镇的某些部分。

sentences.en: It created panic.
sentences.zh: 这造成了恐慌。

sentences.en: The government had attempted involuntary quarantine,
sentences.zh: 政府曾试图进行非自愿隔离，

sentences.en: and they had a really bad experience in the slums of Monrovia.
sentences.zh: 他们在蒙罗维亚的贫民窟里有过非常糟糕的经历。

sentences.en: And so we talked about, you know, is this a viable strategy?
sentences.zh: 所以我们讨论了，你知道的，这真的是一个可行的策略吗？

sentences.en: And we all agreed, no, we can't use involuntary quarantine.
sentences.zh: 我们都一致认为，不行，我们不能使用非自愿隔离。

sentences.en: This is not something that's going to build trust in the community.
sentences.zh: 这不是一件能在社区中建立信任的事情。

sentences.en: It's not a way to manage the outbreak.
sentences.zh: 这不是控制疫情的方法。

sentences.en: People also worried that if they did go into quarantine, they would never come out.
sentences.zh: 人们还担心，如果他们真的被隔离了，就永远也回不来了。

sentences.en: Athelia pointed to the construction of one of the largest Ebola treatment units in Liberia.
sentences.zh: 阿塔利亚指着利比里亚最大的埃博拉治疗中心之一的建设说。

sentences.en: And it was chaotic and difficult, and they built it all, and they forgot to put an exit in.
sentences.zh: 当时情况混乱而艰难，他们把一切都建好了，却忘记留一个出口。

sentences.en: And they didn't build an exit because we weren't thinking about survivors at that time.
sentences.zh: 他们没有建造出口，是因为当时我们根本没有考虑幸存者。

sentences.en: And although this was many months later, many people, understandably so,
sentences.zh: 尽管这是在许多个月之后，但许多人理所当然地认为，

sentences.en: thought that going to an Ebola treatment unit meant that you would not come home.
sentences.zh: 去埃博拉治疗中心就意味着你再也回不了家了。

sentences.en: Dealing with mistrust, the public health officials knew,
sentences.zh: 公共卫生官员知道，应对不信任情绪

sentences.en: was central as they began to trace all the leads of this complex case.
sentences.zh: 是他们开始追踪这一复杂案例所有线索的核心。

sentences.en: As Athelia had been tracking down the health care worker,
sentences.zh: 正当阿塔利亚一直在追踪这名医护人员时，

sentences.en: Frank had been pursuing a different strand of the investigation,
sentences.zh: 弗兰克一直在进行调查的另一条线索，

sentences.en: tracking down the members of the young man's gang.
sentences.zh: 追踪这名年轻人帮派的成员。

sentences.en: This was a community that was not on the best terms with the government.
sentences.zh: 这是一个与政府关系不太融洽的社区。

sentences.en: You know, they were very suspicious of the government.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们对政府非常怀疑。

sentences.en: So it really is a trust-building exercise to go into this community
sentences.zh: 所以进入这个社区拼凑这个故事的所有碎片，实际上是一次建立信任的练习。

sentences.en: to piece together all these pieces of the story.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克和阿塔利亚很快意识到他们能力不及，

sentences.en: Very quickly, Frank and Athelia realized they were in over their heads.
sentences.zh: 他们需要帮助。

sentences.en: They needed help.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们进行调查时，我和这位利比里亚人一起去了。

sentences.en: So when we did the investigation, I went with this Liberian.
sentences.zh: 一位非常出色的利比里亚流行病学家。

sentences.en: Fantastic Liberian epidemiologiSt.
sentences.zh: 一个名叫穆索卡·法拉的人。

sentences.en: Person named Musoka Fala.
sentences.zh: 穆索卡·法拉。

sentences.en: Musoka Fala.
sentences.zh: 我是穆索卡·P。

sentences.en: I am Musoka P.
sentences.zh: 法拉。

sentences.en: Fala.
sentences.zh: 作为一名利比里亚人，穆索卡·法拉对事情的理解比美国人要透彻得多。

sentences.en: As a Liberian, Musoka Fala understood things far better than the Americans.
sentences.zh: 他也对埃博拉的恐怖有着切身的体会。

sentences.en: He also understood the horrors of Ebola firsthand.
sentences.zh: 他也对埃博拉的恐怖有着切身的体会。

sentences.en: The disease had killed his sister.
sentences.zh: 这场疾病夺去了他姐姐的生命。

sentences.en: Musoka's first order of business was to help track down the young men in the gang.
sentences.zh: 莫索卡的首要任务是协助追踪帮派里的年轻成员。

sentences.en: Surprisingly, they weren't hard to find.
sentences.zh: 出人意料的是，他们并不难找。

sentences.en: But they were scared.
sentences.zh: 但他们很害怕。

sentences.en: They were scared, scared that the police, who were still investigating the case as a homicide,
sentences.zh: 他们非常害怕，害怕警察——警方仍在将这起案件作为凶杀案调查——

sentences.en: would arrest them for their role in the knife fight.
sentences.zh: 会因为他们参与了那场刀战而逮捕他们。

sentences.en: The police wanted to go in.
sentences.zh: 警方当时想要强行介入。

sentences.en: However, if we allowed the police to go in, the gangsters would all escape.
sentences.zh: 然而，如果我们允许警方强行进入，帮派分子就会全部逃跑。

sentences.en: And we have pretty close to 35 young men who were all hard-risk contact on the loose.
sentences.zh: 而且我们手头大约有 35 名高危密切接触者在四处游荡。

sentences.en: This is similar to what happened in Panic in the Streets.
sentences.zh: 这类似于电影《街头恐慌》中发生的情节。

sentences.en: Wait a minute.
sentences.zh: 等等。

sentences.en: Wait a minute.
sentences.zh: 等等。

sentences.en: Wait for what?
sentences.zh: 等什么？

sentences.en: Somebody else to die?
sentences.zh: 等另一个人死去吗？

sentences.en: Frank suggested that there should be no arrests.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克建议暂时不要实施逮捕。

sentences.en: Musoka says Frank sat down with the police.
sentences.zh: 莫索卡说，弗兰克与警方坐下来进行了会谈。

sentences.en: He told them that any investigation of the murder would send gang members into hiding
sentences.zh: 他告诉警方，对这起谋杀案的任何调查都会迫使帮派成员藏匿起来，

sentences.en: and potentially spread Ebola further.
sentences.zh: 并可能进一步传播埃博拉病毒。

sentences.en: They should allow the Ebola team to go in and negotiate so that we can have the contact.
sentences.zh: 他们应该允许埃博拉团队进入并进行谈判，这样我们才能控制住密切接触者。

sentences.en: And the police agreed.
sentences.zh: 于是警方同意了。

sentences.en: And the police withdrew their arreSt.
sentences.zh: 警方撤销了逮捕令。

sentences.en: And that's how we went in to negotiate.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们如何得以进去进行谈判的经过。

sentences.en: And this, everyone told us, is what allowed public health officials to start talking to the young men in the gang.
sentences.zh: 每个人都告诉我们，正是这一点，让公共卫生官员得以开始与帮派中的年轻人对话。

sentences.en: So, to recap, public health officials had tracked down the health care worker who treated the young man
sentences.zh: 所以，简而言之，公共卫生官员已经追踪到了治疗这名年轻人的医护人员，

sentences.en: and identified all the people they could tell the young man had come into contact with.
sentences.zh: 并确定了他们所能了解到的这名年轻人曾有过接触的所有人。

sentences.en: The epidemiologists quickly found themselves staring at a growing web.
sentences.zh: 流行病学家们很快发现自己面对着一张不断扩大的交织网络。

sentences.en: There were three important strands.
sentences.zh: 其中有三个关键环节。

sentences.en: First, the young men in the gang would have to be persuaded to enter an Ebola quarantine facility for 21 days.
sentences.zh: 首先，必须说服帮派中的年轻人进入埃博拉隔离设施隔离 21 天。

sentences.en: Second, there was a woman running a drug house who was connected to the gang.
sentences.zh: 其次，有一个经营毒窝的女人，她与这个帮派有牵连。

sentences.en: Gang members were in and out of her home all the time.
sentences.zh: 帮派成员经常出入她的住所。

sentences.en: Most worrisome, the public health officials heard the woman was sick and they thought that she might have Ebola.
sentences.zh: 最让人担忧的是，公共卫生官员听说这个女人病了，他们认为她可能感染了埃博拉。

sentences.en: She had had diarrhea for two days and she was getting sick.
sentences.zh: 她已经腹泻两天了，病情正在加重。

sentences.en: Finally, there was one member of the gang they could not track down.
sentences.zh: 最后，还有一个帮派成员他们怎么也追踪不到。

sentences.en: During the fight, this man had held down the stabbing victim as the blades came out and the blood splattered.
sentences.zh: 在冲突期间，当利刃出鞘、血迹四溅时，正是这个人按住了被刺伤的受害者。

sentences.en: And now, Frank and others found, he'd run away.
sentences.zh: 现在，据弗兰克和其他人发现，他已经逃跑了。

sentences.en: What was his name?
sentences.zh: 他叫什么名字？

sentences.en: His name, ironically, was Time Bomb.
sentences.zh: 讽刺的是，他的名字叫“定时炸弹”。

sentences.en: Coming up, how to stop the outbreak and find Time Bomb.
sentences.zh: 接下来，如何遏制疫情并找到“定时炸弹”。

sentences.en: Stay with us.
sentences.zh: 请继续收听。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantham.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: This week, we're talking about chaos, how we struggle to control it, and why it might sometimes be best to embrace it.
sentences.zh: 本周，我们探讨的是混乱，我们如何挣扎着控制它，以及为什么有时顺其自然可能是最好的选择。

sentences.en: The first story we're telling is about a dangerous kind of chaos in a poor slum in Liberia in 2015.
sentences.zh: 我们要讲的第一个故事发生在 2015 年利比里亚的一个贫困贫民窟，那是一场危险的混乱。

sentences.en: There had been a murder connected to a gang.
sentences.zh: 那里发生了一起与帮派有关的谋杀案。

sentences.en: The victim's body tested positive for Ebola.
sentences.zh: 受害者的遗体埃博拉病毒检测呈阳性。

sentences.en: And now, epidemiologists were in a race against time to stop another outbreak.
sentences.zh: 现在，流行病学家们正与时间赛跑，以阻止另一场疫情爆发。

sentences.en: There were three fires to put out.
sentences.zh: 当时有三处火坑需要扑灭。

sentences.en: An accomplice to the murder, ironically named Time Bomb, had gone missing.
sentences.zh: 谋杀案的一个同伙失踪了，讽刺的是，他的外号叫“定时炸弹”。

sentences.en: The rest of the gang had been identified, but they were reluctant to be quarantined.
sentences.zh: 其余的帮派成员已被查明，但他们不愿意接受隔离。

sentences.en: And then there was the woman known as Drug Mama.
sentences.zh: 还有那个被称为“毒妈”的女人。

sentences.en: She was the godmother of a drug den frequented by members of the gang.
sentences.zh: 她是帮派成员经常光顾的一个毒窟的教母。

sentences.en: She was in her 30s and appeared to have symptoms that suggested Ebola.
sentences.zh: 她三十多岁，似乎出现了暗示感染埃博拉的症状。

sentences.en: If Ebola took hold in her drug den, it would spread very quickly through the community.
sentences.zh: 如果埃博拉在她的毒窟里蔓延，就会在社区里以极快的速度传播开来。

sentences.en: Frank and Mosoka realized they had to quickly run a test to get Drug Mama diagnosed.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克和莫索卡意识到，他们必须迅速进行检测以确诊“毒妈”的病情。

sentences.en: But they anticipated probleMs.
sentences.zh: 但他们预料到了麻烦。

sentences.en: Our dilemma was, how do we approach her such that she accepts us to do an Ebola test?
sentences.zh: 我们的两难境地是：我们该如何接近她，让她接受我们进行埃博拉检测？

sentences.en: The mere mention of Ebola was sending people into a panic.
sentences.zh: 只要一提及埃博拉，人们就会陷入恐慌。

sentences.en: If they told her they were worried she had Ebola, would she vanish and go underground?
sentences.zh: 如果他们告诉她，他们担心她感染了埃博拉，她会不会直接逃跑并销声匿迹？

sentences.en: They didn't want to take the chance.
sentences.zh: 他们不想冒这个险。

sentences.en: So rather than take her into confidence, they decided to trick Drug Mama.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们没有取得她的信任，而是决定对“毒妈”进行欺瞒。

sentences.en: It wasn't ideal, but they were dealing with a crisis.
sentences.zh: 这并不是理想的做法，但他们当时正面临危机。

sentences.en: They had to improvise.
sentences.zh: 他们必须随机应变。

sentences.en: So Frank, being the smart guy he is, we stopped at a pharmacy and we bought her malaria medicine.
sentences.zh: 所以弗兰克不愧是个聪明人，我们在一家药店停下来，为她买了一些治疟疾的药。

sentences.en: And we went there that night and Frank said, I heard you not so well, so we brought you some medicine.
sentences.zh: 那天晚上我们去了她那儿，弗兰克说：“我听说你身体不太舒服，所以我们给你带了点药。”

sentences.en: This is around 9 p.m.
sentences.zh: 当时大约是晚上 9 点。

sentences.en: She said, yes.
sentences.zh: 她说，好的。

sentences.en: So Frank said, take this medicine, I will come back tomorrow and check on you.
sentences.zh: 于是弗兰克说：“吃了吧，我明天再来看你。”

sentences.en: And so the goal was the next morning, we ask for her blood to go check if she had malaria and then we run the Ebola teSt.
sentences.zh: 因此我们的目标是第二天早上要求抽她的血去检查她是否得了疟疾，然后我们再顺便做埃博拉检测。

sentences.en: The trick worked up to a point.
sentences.zh: 这个计策在一定程度上成功了。

sentences.en: The problem was, the next morning, when they took Drug Mama to the hospital to get her blood drawn,
sentences.zh: 问题是，第二天早上，当他们把“毒妈”带到医院去抽血时，

sentences.en: they had to tell health care workers at the hospital what was going on so everyone would take proper precautions.
sentences.zh: 他们不得不把情况告诉医院的医护人员，以便每个人都采取适当的预防措施。

sentences.en: A nurse got scared when they told her they wanted to test for Ebola.
sentences.zh: 当护士听说他们想做埃博拉检测时，吓坏了。

sentences.en: Drug Mama noticed the nurse acting oddly.
sentences.zh: “毒妈”注意到那名护士表现异常。

sentences.en: And then she suspected something else.
sentences.zh: 接着她怀疑发生了别的事。

sentences.en: The Drug Mama left and went back home and became angry with us.
sentences.zh: “毒妈”离开了医院回到了家，并对我们感到生气的。

sentences.en: Musoka and Frank realized the trickery was backfiring.
sentences.zh: 莫索卡和弗兰克意识到这种欺骗手段适得其反了。

sentences.en: So they tried bribery.
sentences.zh: 于是他们尝试了行贿。

sentences.en: We sat down with her, we negotiated, and we told her we'd give her $100 US if she allowed us to do a blood draw at her house.
sentences.zh: 我们坐下来和她谈，进行了协商，并告诉她如果她允许我们在她家里抽血，我们就给她 100 美元。

sentences.en: So we took the blood, and 7 p.m.
sentences.zh: 于是我们抽了血，当晚 7 点，

sentences.en: that night, we got a response that she was negative.
sentences.zh: 我们得到结果，她的检测结果为阴性。

sentences.en: And we all went to bear breathing aside or release.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人都如释重负地松了一口气。

sentences.en: Frank and Musoka turned their focus to the second strand in the web, the young men in the gang.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克和莫索卡将注意力转向了网中的第二个环节——帮派里的年轻人。

sentences.en: Patiently, they explained to the young men that they would be safe from police harassment in the Ebola treatment unit.
sentences.zh: 他们耐心地向这些年轻人解释，在埃博拉治疗中心里，他们将免受警察的骚扰。

sentences.en: We worked it out with them.
sentences.zh: 我们和他们协商好了。

sentences.en: We worked out an arrangement where they, if they agreed to come into the isolation facility, you know, the CDC,
sentences.zh: 我们达成了一项协议：如果他们同意进入隔离设施，你知道的，也就是疾控中心管辖的地方，

sentences.en: I think we ended up paying their families some support costs because they were no longer able to earn money for their families.
sentences.zh: 我想我们最终向他们的家庭提供了一些生活补助，因为他们无法再为家庭赚钱了。

sentences.en: And the government provided the families with food.
sentences.zh: 政府还向这些家庭提供了食物。

sentences.en: And so it worked out really well.
sentences.zh: 所以事情进展得很顺利。

sentences.en: But even this was not enough.
sentences.zh: 但即便如此还是不够。

sentences.en: It turned out some of the young men were drug addicts.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，这些年轻人中有些是瘾君子。

sentences.en: Frank realized he had to keep asking the government to bend the rules in the Ebola treatment unit, or ETU.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克意识到，他必须不断请求政府在埃博拉治疗中心（ETU）破例。

sentences.en: I told the government that we had to anticipate that some of these young men may be drug users,
sentences.zh: 我告诉政府，我们必须预料到这些年轻人中有些人可能会吸毒，

sentences.en: and they may go into withdrawal if we put them in the ETU.
sentences.zh: 如果我们把他们送进治疗中心，他们可能会出现戒断反应。

sentences.en: And, in fact, that was the case.
sentences.zh: 事实也确实如此。

sentences.en: About two to three days later, there were some of them getting agitated.
sentences.zh: 大约两三天后，他们当中有些人开始变得情绪激动。

sentences.en: And somehow they found a way to support their needs for drugs.
sentences.zh: 不知怎的，他们找到了维持毒品需求的方法。

sentences.en: Did you have to do some of that to help them get what they needed to keep them in this facility where they could be quarantined?
sentences.zh: 你们是否不得不做一些那样的事来帮他们获得所需的东西，以便让他们留在可以隔离的设施里？

sentences.en: No, the CDC didn't pay for that or do that.
sentences.zh: 没有，疾控中心没有为此付钱或做那种事。

sentences.en: But the government found a way for the communities to support them.
sentences.zh: 但政府找到了一种让社区支持他们的方法。

sentences.en: So they were doing that.
sentences.zh: 所以他们当时在做这个。

sentences.en: But in some ways, it's sort of an awkward situation for the government,
sentences.zh: 但在某些方面，这对政府来说是一种尴尬的处境，

sentences.en: because in some ways you're asking the government to sort of look the other way while someone's doing something illegal here.
sentences.zh: 因为在某种程度上，你是在要求政府对某些人在这里进行的非法行为睁一只眼闭一只眼。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think that they, but at the same time, it'd be like any withdrawal.
sentences.zh: 我想他们——但与此同时，这也和任何戒断情况一样。

sentences.en: They needed treatment.
sentences.zh: 他们需要治疗。

sentences.en: It wasn't a conventional treatment, that's for sure.
sentences.zh: 这绝不是常规的治疗，那是肯定的。

sentences.en: It was odd for public health officials to be sanctioning illegal drug use.
sentences.zh: 公共卫生官员竟然默许非法吸毒，这确实很怪异。

sentences.en: But again, when you're in the middle of an unfolding catastrophe, you sometimes have to bend the rules.
sentences.zh: 但话又说回来，当你身处一场正在发生的灾难之中时，有时你不得不打破常规。

sentences.en: Even though CDC wasn't actually supplying anyone drugs, the arrangement produced lots of double-takes.
sentences.zh: 尽管疾控中心实际上并没有向任何人提供毒品，但这种安排还是让人大跌眼镜。

sentences.en: One day, a Liberian government minister turned to Frank during a discussion and joked about the backdoor drug channel.
sentences.zh: 有一天，利比里亚政府的一位部长在讨论中转向弗兰克，开玩笑地谈到了这个后门毒品渠道。

sentences.en: And he says, and I understand that CDC is providing them with the marijuana.
sentences.zh: 他说：“我听说疾控中心正在给他们提供大麻。”

sentences.en: And I said, excuse me, sir.
sentences.zh: 我说：“不好意思，先生。”

sentences.en: He said, I'd like to correct that.
sentences.zh: 他说：“我想纠正一下。”

sentences.en: He said, CDC is not providing the marijuana, but we're providing the cocaine.
sentences.zh: 他说：“疾控中心提供的不是大麻，我们提供的是可卡因。”

sentences.en: Incredibly, the epidemiologists actually managed to quarantine the gang members.
sentences.zh: 令人难以置信的是，流行病学家们竟然成功地将帮派成员隔离了。

sentences.en: These were young men who no one thought would listen to the authorities.
sentences.zh: 这些都是原本以为根本不会听从当局安排的年轻人。

sentences.en: But by reposing trust in them and treating the young men as partners,
sentences.zh: 但通过对他们寄予信任并把这些年轻人当作伙伴对待，

sentences.en: the public health officials had found a solution that seemed to work better than coercion or trickery.
sentences.zh: 公共卫生官员找到了一种似乎比强迫或欺骗更有效的解决方案。

sentences.en: Still, this wasn't the end.
sentences.zh: 不过，这还没完。

sentences.en: There was a third strand of the web they had to track down.
sentences.zh: 还有网中的第三个环节需要他们去追踪。

sentences.en: Time bomb.
sentences.zh: 定时炸弹。

sentences.en: Time bomb became very elusive.
sentences.zh: 定时炸弹变得非常难以捉摸。

sentences.en: We could not find time bomb.
sentences.zh: 我们找不到定时炸弹。

sentences.en: At first, gang members did not want to tell Mosoka or Frank where time bomb was.
sentences.zh: 起初，帮派成员不愿意告诉莫索卡或弗兰克“定时炸弹”在哪里。

sentences.en: But as we built friendship and rapport with the other criminals, one of them took us to his house.
sentences.zh: 但随着我们与这些罪犯建立起友谊和融洽关系，其中一个人带我们去了他的住所。

sentences.en: There, they found a young man, a young woman, and a baby.
sentences.zh: 在那里，他们找到了一个年轻男子、一个年轻女人和一个婴儿。

sentences.en: The epidemiologist asked the young man if he was time bomb.
sentences.zh: 流行病学家问这个年轻人他是不是“定时炸弹”。

sentences.en: He said, I'm not time bomb.
sentences.zh: 他说：“我不是定时炸弹。”

sentences.en: Time bomb is going out.
sentences.zh: “定时炸弹外出了。”

sentences.en: I'm his younger brother.
sentences.zh: “我是他弟弟。”

sentences.en: But if he comes back, I will let you know.
sentences.zh: “但他如果回来，我会通知你们的。”

sentences.en: Then I said, OK, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 然后我说：“好的，非常感谢。”

sentences.en: It was at this point that Mosoka and Frank did something very kind and very wise that led to a breakthrough in the case.
sentences.zh: 正是在这个时候，莫索卡和弗兰克做了一件非常仁慈且非常明智的事，从而促成了案件的突破。

sentences.en: His wife had a young baby.
sentences.zh: 他的妻子带着一个小婴儿。

sentences.en: And I remember giving the wife $100 and said, go ahead and buy milk for the baby.
sentences.zh: 我记得我给了那个妻子 100 美元，并说道：“拿着去给孩子买点奶粉吧。”

sentences.en: Feed the baby and we'll take care of you.
sentences.zh: “把孩子喂饱，我们会照顾你们的。”

sentences.en: Something changed in the young man's demeanor.
sentences.zh: 这个年轻人的态度发生了某种变化。

sentences.en: After I did that, he turned to me and said to me, I am time bomb.
sentences.zh: 我这么做之后，他转向我，对我说：“我就是定时炸弹。”

sentences.en: Frank and Mosoka told time bomb and his wife that they would be back that night.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克和莫索卡告诉“定时炸弹”和他的妻子，他们当晚会回来。

sentences.en: They promised they would return with more food.
sentences.zh: 他们承诺会带更多的食物回来。

sentences.en: Frank came to me with the food and said, Mosoka, we need to go to meet this guy.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克带着食物来找我，说：“莫索卡，我们需要去见这个人。”

sentences.en: This was in the ghetto.
sentences.zh: 这里是贫民窟。

sentences.en: I went with Mosoka and it was like 10 o'clock at night.
sentences.zh: 我跟莫索卡一起去了，当时大约是晚上 10 点。

sentences.en: There was no electricity.
sentences.zh: 那里没有电。

sentences.en: This place was pitch black.
sentences.zh: 这个地方漆黑一片。

sentences.en: We had to go and drive to the grass.
sentences.zh: 我们不得不把车开进草丛里。

sentences.en: This was like a slump community.
sentences.zh: 这就像是一个贫民窟社区。

sentences.en: It's known to have gangsters.
sentences.zh: 这里以帮派分子出没而闻名。

sentences.en: And that's what Frank was emphasizing that we had to keep our word.
sentences.zh: 这就是弗兰克一直强调的：我们必须言出必行。

sentences.en: They had to trust us.
sentences.zh: 他们必须信任我们。

sentences.en: This was the key.
sentences.zh: 这正是关键所在。

sentences.en: So we brought food to him and his family.
sentences.zh: 于是我们带了食物给他和他的家人。

sentences.en: I think a couple of sacks of rice and things.
sentences.zh: 我想大概是几麻袋大米之类的东西。

sentences.en: As we walked towards them and they saw us coming with rice on our shoulder, for some reason
sentences.zh: 当我们朝他们走去，而他们看到我们扛着大米走来时，不知为什么

sentences.en: they trusted us and they came to the car and helped us take the rice.
sentences.zh: 他们信任了我们，走到车边帮我们搬大米。

sentences.en: Frank and Mosoka gently asked time bomb whether he was willing to come to the Ebola treatment
sentences.zh: 弗兰克和莫索卡温和地询问“定时炸弹”是否愿意去埃博拉治疗

sentences.en: facility to be quarantined.
sentences.zh: 中心接受隔离。

sentences.en: Time bomb said he wasn't ready to do that.
sentences.zh: “定时炸弹”说他还没准备好这么做。

sentences.en: Frank and Mosoka said they understood that they were willing to trust him to do the right
sentences.zh: 弗兰克和莫索卡表示他们理解，他们愿意相信他会做正确的

sentences.en: thing.
sentences.zh: 事。

sentences.en: If you get sick, you call us.
sentences.zh: 如果你病了，就给我们打电话。

sentences.en: And he said, I will do that.
sentences.zh: 他说，我会的。

sentences.en: I trust you guys.
sentences.zh: 我相信你们。

sentences.en: And so I think it was a matter of building up trust and comfort level for him to talk
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得这是一个建立信任和舒适感的过程，好让他愿意与

sentences.en: to us.
sentences.zh: 我们交谈。

sentences.en: In the end, none of the young gang members contracted Ebola, not even time bomb.
sentences.zh: 最后，年轻帮派成员中没有人感染埃博拉，连“定时炸弹”也没有。

sentences.en: The cluster did not spread in the ghetto.
sentences.zh: 疫情并未在贫民窟蔓延。

sentences.en: Drug mama recovered from her illness.
sentences.zh: “毒妈”从病中康复了。

sentences.en: Only one person connected with the cluster was affected.
sentences.zh: 只有一名与该群聚感染相关的人受到了影响。

sentences.en: The medical worker who'd sutured up the young man's wounds, the one that went into hiding
sentences.zh: 那个给年轻人缝合伤口的医护人员，就是阿塔莉亚跟他谈过话后

sentences.en: after Athalia talked to him?
sentences.zh: 躲起来的那个人？

sentences.en: He came down with Ebola-related symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 他出现了埃博拉相关症状。

sentences.en: Eventually, he did seek treatment.
sentences.zh: 最终，他确实去寻求治疗了。

sentences.en: But it was too late.
sentences.zh: 但为时已晚。

sentences.en: He died, unfortunately, in the Ebola treatment unit.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，他在埃博拉治疗中心去世了。

sentences.en: We started today's episode with a 1950 movie, Panic in the Streets.
sentences.zh: 我们今天的节目从一部 1950 年的电影《街头恐慌》开始。

sentences.en: At the end of that movie, the hero, a public health worker, ends up in a warehouse with the
sentences.zh: 在那部电影的结尾，男主角——一名公共卫生工作者——与携带着

sentences.en: criminals who are carrying the deadly plague.
sentences.zh: 致命瘟疫的罪犯一起被困在一个仓库里。

sentences.en: He pleads for them to hand over their guns.
sentences.zh: 他恳求他们交出枪支。

sentences.en: But they get into a climactic shootout and the criminals are killed.
sentences.zh: 但他们陷入了一场高潮迭起的枪战，罪犯被击毙了。

sentences.en: The public health workers in Liberia never solved things with guns.
sentences.zh: 利比里亚的公共卫生工作者从来不用枪来解决问题。

sentences.en: And really, when it came down to it, Athalia says, they achieved some of their best results
sentences.zh: 说真的，正如阿塔莉亚所说，归根结底，他们取得的一些最佳成果

sentences.en: without coercion or trickery.
sentences.zh: 并没有使用强迫或欺骗手段。

sentences.en: Building those invisible but very real bonds of trust took time, but it was essential to
sentences.zh: 建立那些隐形却又真实存在的信任纽带需要时间，但这对

sentences.en: stopping an outbreak.
sentences.zh: 阻止疫情爆发至关重要。

sentences.en: When it comes down to what we were asking people to do, either to trust the health care system
sentences.zh: 说到我们要求人们做的事情，无论是信任医疗系统

sentences.en: or to trust the government enough to agree to this voluntary precautionary isolation, that's
sentences.zh: 还是足够信任政府以同意这种自愿的预防性隔离，这都是

sentences.en: an extraordinarily difficult thing to do.
sentences.zh: 一件极其困难的事情。

sentences.en: You're asking people to leave their friends and family for 21 days, or we were asking people
sentences.zh: 你要求人们离开亲朋好友 21 天，或者我们要求人们

sentences.en: to change their burial custoMs.
sentences.zh: 改变他们的葬礼习俗。

sentences.en: And it's difficult.
sentences.zh: 这很难。

sentences.en: It can sound simple.
sentences.zh: 听起来可能很简单。

sentences.en: And I know that I spoke to people here who would say, I don't understand.
sentences.zh: 我知道我在这里跟一些人聊过，他们会说，我不明白。

sentences.en: Why can't they just change the way they bury the dead?
sentences.zh: 为什么他们就不能改变埋葬死者的方式呢？

sentences.en: Or change the way they care for their family members if they're sick.
sentences.zh: 或者如果家人生病了，为什么不能改变照顾他们的方式。

sentences.en: But as a mother, I can't imagine not touching my child if he was sick and not trying to
sentences.zh: 但作为母亲，我无法想象如果我的孩子生病了却不去碰触他，不去尝试

sentences.en: provide comfort.
sentences.zh: 给予他安慰。

sentences.en: So it's really understanding what it is that's driving people.
sentences.zh: 所以，真正要去理解的是究竟是什么在驱动着人们。

sentences.en: You have to understand their context, their concerns, and their needs.
sentences.zh: 你必须了解他们的处境、他们的担忧和他们的需求。

sentences.en: I think it's about interpersonal relationships.
sentences.zh: 我认为这关乎人际关系。

sentences.en: You have to be honest and straightforward about what you need and why.
sentences.zh: 你需要开诚布公地说明你需要什么以及为什么需要。

sentences.en: And most importantly, I think you need to be human.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，我认为你需要展现人性。

sentences.en: So much of being human is chaos.
sentences.zh: 人性的很大一部分就是混乱。

sentences.en: The doctors in Liberia found an innovative way to try and fight it.
sentences.zh: 利比里亚的医生们找到了一种创新方法来尝试对抗它。

sentences.en: In fact, that's what we usually do when it comes to chaos.
sentences.zh: 事实上，每当面对混乱时，我们通常都是这么做的。

sentences.en: We try to find ways to control it, to manage it.
sentences.zh: 我们试图寻找控制它、管理它的方法。

sentences.en: If you're a parent, you've probably told your kids a thousand times,
sentences.zh: 如果你是父母，你可能已经对孩子说过一千遍了：

sentences.en: your room is a mess, clean it up.
sentences.zh: 你的房间真乱，把它收拾干净。

sentences.en: Managers tell their employees to get organized.
sentences.zh: 管理者让员工们把工作理出头绪。

sentences.en: Here in the United States, we elect presidents to go clean up Washington.
sentences.zh: 在美国，我们选举总统来整顿华盛顿。

sentences.en: In the next half of our show today, we explore a very different idea.
sentences.zh: 在今天节目的后半部分，我们将探讨一个截然不同的想法。

sentences.en: What happens if we treat chaos as our friend instead of our enemy?
sentences.zh: 如果我们把混乱当成朋友而不是敌人，会发生什么？

sentences.en: Tim Harford believes we should do just that.
sentences.zh: 蒂姆·哈福德认为我们应该这样做。

sentences.en: He's the author of Messy, The Power of Disorder to Transform Our Lives.
sentences.zh: 他是《混乱：杂乱无章如何改变我们的生活》一书的作者。

sentences.en: He joined us recently for a live taping.
sentences.zh: 他最近参加了我们的现场录制。

sentences.en: We were just blocks from the White House at NPR's Weekend in Washington.
sentences.zh: 我们就在离白宫几个街区远的华盛顿 NPR 周末活动现场。

sentences.en: It's an annual event that brings together public radio fans and supporters.
sentences.zh: 这是一个每年举办一次的活动，汇聚了公共广播的粉丝和支持者。

sentences.en: Tim Harford, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 蒂姆·哈福德，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Thank you very much, Shankar.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢，尚卡尔。

sentences.en: I want to begin by playing you a piece of music, Tim.
sentences.zh: 蒂姆，我想先放一段音乐给你听。

sentences.en: How did that piece of music come about?
sentences.zh: 这段音乐是怎么来的？

sentences.en: What's the story?
sentences.zh: 背后有什么故事吗？

sentences.en: It's beautiful, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 很美，对吧？

sentences.en: Two of my children were born to that.
sentences.zh: 我的两个孩子伴随着这首曲子出生。

sentences.en: It was played by Keith Jarrett, a great jazz pianist, in 1975 in Cologne.
sentences.zh: 它是由伟大的爵士钢琴家基思·贾雷特于 1975 年在科隆演奏的。

sentences.en: And if you had been there two or three hours before the concert, you would not have expected things to go well.
sentences.zh: 如果你在音乐会开始前两三个小时去到现场，你绝对不会预料到事情会一切顺利。

sentences.en: Keith Jarrett had just refused to play.
sentences.zh: 基思·贾雷特刚刚拒绝演奏。

sentences.en: And the reason he'd refused to play is because he had arrived on stage, met the piano.
sentences.zh: 他拒绝演奏的原因是，他到达舞台后，见到了那架钢琴。

sentences.en: He was supposed to be completely improvised, by the way.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一下，这场演出本来应该完全是即兴的。

sentences.en: The whole thing was going to be improvised.
sentences.zh: 整场音乐会都将是即兴创作。

sentences.en: Met this piano and realized that there'd been a mistake.
sentences.zh: 结果见到这架钢琴，他意识到弄错了。

sentences.en: And the thing was literally unplayable.
sentences.zh: 这东西简直没法弹。

sentences.en: It was out of tune.
sentences.zh: 它走音了。

sentences.en: Black keys were sticking.
sentences.zh: 黑键按下去卡住弹不上来。

sentences.en: The pedals didn't work.
sentences.zh: 踏板失灵。

sentences.en: The upper register of the keyboard was harsh and tinny because all the felt had worn away.
sentences.zh: 键盘的高音区听起来刺耳又单薄，因为所有的毛毡都磨损殆尽了。

sentences.en: And most importantly, it was too small.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，它声音太小了。

sentences.en: So it didn't have enough volume to actually reach the back of the Cologne Auditorium.
sentences.zh: 所以音量根本不足以传到科隆音乐厅的最后排。

sentences.en: And so, of course, he refused to play.
sentences.zh: 因此，他当然拒绝演奏。

sentences.en: And the organizer of the concert, who was this young German girl, she's just 17 years old,
sentences.zh: 音乐会的组织者是一个年轻的德国女孩，年仅 17 岁，

sentences.en: desperately tried to fix the piano, to replace the piano.
sentences.zh: 她绝望地试图修理钢琴，试图更换钢琴。

sentences.en: She managed to get it somewhat in tune.
sentences.zh: 她设法让音准稍微恢复了一点。

sentences.en: But basically, she couldn't really improve on it.
sentences.zh: 但基本上，她没法真正改善它的状况。

sentences.en: And she couldn't get it replaced.
sentences.zh: 而且她也没能弄到一台新钢琴来替换。

sentences.en: And so the only option she had was to beg Keith Jarrett to play.
sentences.zh: 所以她唯一的选择就是恳求基思·贾雷特弹奏。

sentences.en: And, of course, he saw this teenager, thought of the 1,400 people who were about to show up
sentences.zh: 当然，他看到这个十几岁的女孩，想到了即将到场

sentences.en: and listen to the concert, and said to her, never forget.
sentences.zh: 聆听音乐会的 1400 名观众，便对她说：永远别忘了一件事。

sentences.en: Only for you.
sentences.zh: 只为你而弹。

sentences.en: And he went on stage, and he and his producer recorded the concert because they wanted documentary evidence of what a musical catastrophe sounds like
sentences.zh: 于是他上了台，他和制作人录下了这场音乐会，因为他们想留下纪录片证据，记录下音乐灾难听起来是什么样的，

sentences.en: so they could play it to future promoters to tell them to do a good job and get a proper piano.
sentences.zh: 这样他们就可以把它播放给未来的演出主办方听，好告诉他们要做好工作并准备一架像样的钢琴。

sentences.en: But, in fact, it's a masterpiece.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，这是一部杰作。

sentences.en: It's Keith Jarrett's most popular work.
sentences.zh: 这是基思·贾雷特最受欢迎的作品。

sentences.en: In fact, it's the best-selling jazz album in history, solo jazz album in history.
sentences.zh: 事实上，它是历史上最畅销的爵士专辑，历史上最畅销的独奏爵士专辑。

sentences.en: And the best-selling piano album in history is the Colne Concert.
sentences.zh: 历史上最畅销的钢琴专辑就是《科隆音乐会》。

sentences.en: And the surprising thing is that all the adjustments that Jarrett had to make to cope with this bad piano made the music better.
sentences.zh: 令人惊讶的是，贾雷特为了应付这架破钢琴而做出所有的调整，反而让音乐变得更好了。

sentences.en: So he avoided the harsh upper registers.
sentences.zh: 所以他避开了刺耳的高音区。

sentences.en: He stuck to the middle of the keyboard.
sentences.zh: 他一直局限在键盘的中部弹奏。

sentences.en: That makes it sound very soothing.
sentences.zh: 这使得它听起来非常舒缓。

sentences.en: But he also had to compensate for the fact that the piano was so quiet.
sentences.zh: 但他也必须弥补这架钢琴声音太轻的缺陷。

sentences.en: So he had these rolling, repetitive riffs in the bass to try to get some resonance.
sentences.zh: 因此，他在低音区加入了这种连绵、重复的即兴重复段，以获得一些共鸣。

sentences.en: And he also just stood up and pounded down on the keys.
sentences.zh: 而且他还站起身来用力砸击琴键。

sentences.en: So you can hear him moaning in frustration during the concert.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以在音乐会期间听到他沮丧地呻吟。

sentences.en: He's hating it.
sentences.zh: 他恨透了这架琴。

sentences.en: But it is amazing.
sentences.zh: 但它确实令人惊叹。

sentences.en: And that combination of the peacefulness and the dynamism makes this electrifying piece of music.
sentences.zh: 那种平静感与动感结合在一起，造就了一首令人电光石火般震撼的音乐。

sentences.en: So he did not expect that a bad piano would produce a great concert.
sentences.zh: 所以他绝对没料到一架破钢琴能弹出一场伟大的音乐会。

sentences.en: But, in fact, it did.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，它确实做到了。

sentences.en: And the argument in my book is very often we're faced with the unplayable piano.
sentences.zh: 我书中的观点是，我们经常会遇到那架无法弹奏的钢琴。

sentences.en: And actually, we produce something great out of it.
sentences.zh: 而事实上，我们能从中创造出伟大的成果。

sentences.en: You have a number of examples besides Keith Jarrett about how disruptions and inconveniences and surprises can sometimes have paradoxically good effects on us,
sentences.zh: 除了基思·贾雷特之外，你还有许多例子，说明中断、不便和意外有时会给我们带来悖论般的好处，

sentences.en: even though we all try to avoid those disruptions.
sentences.zh: 尽管我们都在极力避免这些中断。

sentences.en: You talk about commuters, for example, who suddenly have to find a new way to work,
sentences.zh: 比如，你谈到了通勤者，他们突然不得不寻找一条上班的新路线，

sentences.en: or scientists who are working on so many projects that they are discombobulated because they don't know what they're working on.
sentences.zh: 或者科学家们同时进行太多项目，以至于他们手忙脚乱，因为他们不知道自己在忙些什么。

sentences.en: In many of these cases, you find that disorder and confusion could actually be helpful.
sentences.zh: 在许多这类案例中，你会发现混乱和迷惑其实是有益的。

sentences.en: Yeah, so in the case of commuters, there was a transport strike in London a couple of years ago.
sentences.zh: 是的，以通勤者为例，几年前伦敦发生了一场交通罢工。

sentences.en: Shut down not all, but most of the London Underground stations for 48 hours.
sentences.zh: 导致伦敦地铁并非全部、但绝大部分车站关闭了 48 小时。

sentences.en: So not a long strike.
sentences.zh: 所以罢工时间并不长。

sentences.en: But most commuters in London use public transport.
sentences.zh: 但伦敦大多数通勤者都使用公共交通。

sentences.en: It's not really set up for the car.
sentences.zh: 这里其实并不太适合开车。

sentences.en: But you could travel on the bus.
sentences.zh: 不过你可以坐公交车。

sentences.en: There are overground trains.
sentences.zh: 还有地上铁列车。

sentences.en: Or you could use some of the tube lines that were not shut down.
sentences.zh: 或者你也可以使用那些没有关闭的地铁线路。

sentences.en: There are various other options.
sentences.zh: 还有各种其他选择。

sentences.en: And economists who studied this got hold of the data as to the trips that people were making.
sentences.zh: 研究这一现象的经济学家获取了人们出行行程的数据。

sentences.en: They identified people who took the same route to work every single day.
sentences.zh: 他们找出了那些每天都走同一条路线去上班的人。

sentences.en: Well, there's a technical term for this.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这有一个专业术语。

sentences.en: It's called commuters.
sentences.zh: 叫做通勤者。

sentences.en: And you would think that these are the people who have absolutely perfected their route to work.
sentences.zh: 你可能会认为，这些人绝对已经把上班路线练到了炉火纯青的地步。

sentences.en: Surely commuters, they know every step.
sentences.zh: 通勤者肯定知道每一个步骤。

sentences.en: They know where to stand on the platform, which track.
sentences.zh: 他们知道该在站台的哪个位置、哪条轨道上等车。

sentences.en: And yet, the economists found, looking at the people who took the same route to work every day, who then changed their route during the strike, thousands of them, about 5%,
sentences.zh: 然而，经济学家通过观察那些每天走同一条上班路线、却在罢工期间改变了路线的人发现，成千上万的人中，大约有 5%，

sentences.en: thousands upon thousands, stayed with the new route.
sentences.zh: 成千上万的人，最终留在了新路线上。

sentences.en: So, these are people, this is the optimum population for having honed their route to perfection.
sentences.zh: 所以，这些人，他们是把通勤路线磨练到完美状态的典型人群。

sentences.en: And yet, 1 in 20 of them discovered that when they were forced to find a new way, they found a better way.
sentences.zh: 然而，每 20 个人中就有 1 人发现，当他们被迫寻找新路线时，他们找到了一条更好的路线。

sentences.en: And I think that that's quite a common situation.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一种相当普遍的情况。

sentences.en: We get into particular habits, whether it's creative or whether it's just trying to get to work.
sentences.zh: 我们养成了特定的习惯，无论是为了创作还是仅仅为了去上班。

sentences.en: We get into a particular habit.
sentences.zh: 我们陷入了某种特定的习惯。

sentences.en: We're knocked off course.
sentences.zh: 然后我们被打乱了节奏。

sentences.en: And very often, of course, our original habit was the right way to do things, and we go back.
sentences.zh: 当然，很多时候我们原本的习惯才是做事的最优解，于是我们又回去了。

sentences.en: But often enough to be useful, we find that the new way of doing things is actually better all along.
sentences.zh: 但频率足够高的是，我们往往会发现，新的做事方式其实从一开始就更好。

sentences.en: And if only we'd been forced into it, we would have discovered that years ago.
sentences.zh: 而且如果我们早被逼着这么做，我们几年前就发现了。

sentences.en: One of the things I want to do in this conversation is try and tease apart when messiness can be our friend and when it can be our enemy.
sentences.zh: 我想在这场对话中探讨的事情之一，就是试着厘清什么时候杂乱能成为我们的朋友，什么时候它会成为我们的敌人。

sentences.en: There's a reason many of us try and avoid messiness.
sentences.zh: 我们许多人试图避免杂乱是有原因的。

sentences.en: It's because messiness causes delays.
sentences.zh: 那是因为杂乱会导致延误。

sentences.en: It causes disruptions.
sentences.zh: 它会导致中断。

sentences.en: You end up being late for some things.
sentences.zh: 结果就是你做某些事情会迟到。

sentences.en: And I'm wondering, as I read some of the examples in your book, whether it was the case that messiness helps people who actually have a base of preparation.
sentences.zh: 我在阅读你书中的一些例子时就在想，是不是只有在人们本身就具备一定准备基础的情况下，杂乱才能帮到他们？

sentences.en: So in other words, Keith Jarrett, he's a professional musician.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，就像基思·贾瑞特，他是一名专业音乐家。

sentences.en: He's very gifted.
sentences.zh: 他极具天赋。

sentences.en: He's practiced, and he's learned the rules of how to play a proper piano for years and years and years.
sentences.zh: 他练习过，并且多年来一直学习如何正确弹奏钢琴的规则。

sentences.en: You place me before that piano, and what you're going to hear is not genius.
sentences.zh: 如果你把我放在那架钢琴前，你听到的绝不是天才。

sentences.en: What you're going to hear is just a mess.
sentences.zh: 你听到的只是一团糟。

sentences.en: And the reason Keith Jarrett could adapt was because he had the base of knowing the rules to now say, I can throw out the rule book and create something brilliant.
sentences.zh: 基思·贾瑞特之所以能够适应，是因为他有着掌握规则的基础，从而现在能说：我可以抛开规则手册，创作出精彩绝伦的作品。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's absolutely right, Shankar.
sentences.zh: 是的，我觉得完全正确，香卡。

sentences.en: Is it okay?
sentences.zh: 可以吗？

sentences.en: Can I open a big bag of complexity science on you?
sentences.zh: 我能向你抛出一大堆复杂的科学理论吗？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 当然可以。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So basically, if you are trying to solve a very complex problem, we have various algorithms that try to solve this.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，如果你正试图解决一个非常复杂的问题，我们有各种算法来尝试解决它。

sentences.en: And I'll come to the question of skill in a second.
sentences.zh: 我一会儿就会谈到技巧的问题。

sentences.en: The algorithms, computer algorithms searching for solutions in a very, very complex problem space.
sentences.zh: 这些算法，也就是在极其复杂的问题空间中寻找解决方案的计算机算法。

sentences.en: One possible approach is to look for step-by-step improvements.
sentences.zh: 一种可能的方案是寻找逐步的改进。

sentences.en: So that's the equivalent of skill.
sentences.zh: 这就相当于技巧。

sentences.en: You are looking for step-by-step improvements to get from a bad solution to a better solution and a better one and a better one and a better one.
sentences.zh: 你在寻找循序渐进的改进，从一个糟糕的解决方案到一个更好的方案，再到一个更好的，又一个更好的，一直下去。

sentences.en: And eventually, you find the perfect solution.
sentences.zh: 最终，你找到了完美的解决方案。

sentences.en: It turns out that way of looking at complex problems doesn't usually work.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，这种看待复杂问题的方式通常行不通。

sentences.en: And the reason is, the algorithm, as it looks for these small improvements, gets stuck.
sentences.zh: 原因在于，算法在寻找这些微小改进的过程中会卡住。

sentences.en: So these algorithms that search for solutions, they work much better if you add random shocks.
sentences.zh: 因此，这些搜寻解决方案的算法，如果加入随机冲击，效果会好得多。

sentences.en: Lots of different ways to do that.
sentences.zh: 有很多不同的方法可以做到这一点。

sentences.en: But basically, for most of the kind of problem I'm discussing, a computer scientist would approach it by saying,
sentences.zh: 但基本上，对于我所讨论的大多数问题，计算机科学家的处理方法会是：

sentences.en: we're going to have the step-by-step quest for improvements, but we're also going to have lots of randomness, lots of shocks.
sentences.zh: 我们将进行逐步寻找改进的过程，但同时我们也会引入大量的随机性，大量的冲击。

sentences.en: Just keep knocking the algorithm off course, because then it won't get stuck.
sentences.zh: 不断地把算法撞离正轨，因为这样它就不会卡住了。

sentences.en: So now we come back to Keith Jarrett.
sentences.zh: 现在我们回到基思·贾瑞特。

sentences.en: He's like an algorithm that's searching for step-by-step improvements.
sentences.zh: 他就像一个寻找逐步改进的算法。

sentences.en: He's a great musician.
sentences.zh: 他是一位伟大的音乐家。

sentences.en: He's always looking for the perfect concert.
sentences.zh: 他一直在寻找完美的音乐会。

sentences.en: Clearly, he's a very creative person, because he's improvising every night.
sentences.zh: 显然，他是一个极具创造力的人，因为他每天晚上都在即兴演奏。

sentences.en: But he always starts with a good piano.
sentences.zh: 但他总是从一架好钢琴开始。

sentences.en: Always.
sentences.zh: 总是如此。

sentences.en: And then this one night where they say, you know what, Keith, 12 of these notes don't work, and you should probably avoid most of that part.
sentences.zh: 然后有天晚上，有人对他说：你知道吗，基思，这其中的12个音符不管用，你大概应该避开那大部分区域。

sentences.en: And that thing with the pedals don't do that either.
sentences.zh: 还有那个踏板的事情，也别那样用。

sentences.en: But then he sits down at the piano, and then his skill kicks in, and he's looking for the incremental improvements.
sentences.zh: 但接着他在钢琴前坐下，然后他的技巧开始发挥作用，他开始寻找渐进式的改进。

sentences.en: He's looking for a path to find great music.
sentences.zh: 他在寻找通往美妙音乐的途径。

sentences.en: And he finds it.
sentences.zh: 他找到了。

sentences.en: So yes, you need skill, but the random shocks help.
sentences.zh: 所以是的，你需要技巧，但随机冲击会有所帮助。

sentences.en: So for all the children who are listening to this podcast, I want to make clear that you're not saying
sentences.zh: 因此，对于所有收听这个播客的孩子们，我想明确一点：你并不是在说

sentences.en: that every time your parent tells you to clean up the room, you should just say,
sentences.zh: 每当你的父母让你打扫房间时，你就可以说：

sentences.en: Tim Harford says I shouldn't.
sentences.zh: 蒂姆·哈福德说我不该打扫。

sentences.en: Well, I have to say, since writing the book, I have stopped asking my children to clear up their room.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我必须得说，自从写了这本书后，我再也没有要求过我的孩子们清理房间。

sentences.en: And the reason is, the reason is, I read an amazing study that had been conducted by two British psychologists,
sentences.zh: 原因在于，原因在于，我读到了一项由两位英国心理学家进行的惊人研究，

sentences.en: Alex Haslam and Craig Knight.
sentences.zh: 亚历克斯·哈斯勒姆和克雷格·奈特。

sentences.en: What they did was, it wasn't anything to do with children, but it was to do with clean desk policies.
sentences.zh: 他们的实验与儿童无关，而是关于整洁办公桌政策的。

sentences.en: They got people to sit down and work in artificial office environments.
sentences.zh: 他们让人坐在人工办公环境中工作并进行记录。

sentences.en: You know, we've created an office for you.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们为你打造了一间办公室。

sentences.en: Here are some tasks.
sentences.zh: 这里有一些任务。

sentences.en: Sort this paperwork.
sentences.zh: 整理这些文件。

sentences.en: Do these puzzles.
sentences.zh: 做这些拼图。

sentences.en: Handle these emails.
sentences.zh: 处理这些电子邮件。

sentences.en: Regular sort of knowledge worker tasks.
sentences.zh: 常规的知识型工作任务。

sentences.en: Standard stuff.
sentences.zh: 标准的东西。

sentences.en: And they measured how well people did.
sentences.zh: 他们衡量了人们的表现。

sentences.en: And there were four different arms to this experiment.
sentences.zh: 这个实验有四个不同的方向。

sentences.en: People were randomized into different arMs.
sentences.zh: 人们被随机分到不同的组别。

sentences.en: So in one case, the office was very, very minimaliSt.
sentences.zh: 所以在第一种情况下，办公室非常非常简约。

sentences.en: Just a chair, you know, pencil, paper, no distractions.
sentences.zh: 只有一把椅子，你知道的，铅笔、纸张，没有任何干扰。

sentences.en: People did fine in that.
sentences.zh: 人们在那里表现得还不错。

sentences.en: They didn't really like it.
sentences.zh: 他们其实并不太喜欢。

sentences.en: On average, suits some people.
sentences.zh: 平均而言，这适合某些人。

sentences.en: The second approach, there were more decorations in the office.
sentences.zh: 第二种方法，办公室里的装饰更多一些。

sentences.en: There were pot plants.
sentences.zh: 有盆栽植物。

sentences.en: There were posters.
sentences.zh: 有海报。

sentences.en: You know, some distractions, but it felt friendlier.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，有一些干扰，但感觉更友好。

sentences.en: People liked that more.
sentences.zh: 人们更喜欢这样。

sentences.en: But here's the real kicker to this research.
sentences.zh: 但这项研究真正绝妙的地方在这里。

sentences.en: The other two treatments, the other two parts of the research.
sentences.zh: 另外两种处理方式，也就是研究的另外两个部分。

sentences.en: First, the researchers said, you can organize this office how you like.
sentences.zh: 首先，研究人员说：你可以按照自己喜欢的方式布置这间办公室。

sentences.en: Bring in the posters.
sentences.zh: 把海报挂进来。

sentences.en: Send away the posters.
sentences.zh: 把海报拿走。

sentences.en: Put the pot plants where you like.
sentences.zh: 把盆栽放在你喜欢的地方。

sentences.en: Or if you want, we'll take the pot plants away from you.
sentences.zh: 或者如果你愿意，我们可以把盆栽拿走。

sentences.en: However you want.
sentences.zh: 随你高兴。

sentences.en: People loved that.
sentences.zh: 人们太喜欢这样了。

sentences.en: They got so much more done.
sentences.zh: 他们完成了多得多的工作。

sentences.en: They felt happier.
sentences.zh: 他们感到更快乐。

sentences.en: They were more productive.
sentences.zh: 他们的生产力更高。

sentences.en: Significantly more productive.
sentences.zh: 生产力显著提高。

sentences.en: In the fourth part of the trial, they did that.
sentences.zh: 在实验的第四部分，他们做了这样的事。

sentences.en: They said, arrange it however you like.
sentences.zh: 他们说：随心所欲地布置吧。

sentences.en: And then the experimenter came in and said, well, I'm sorry, this isn't appropriate for
sentences.zh: 然后实验人员走进来，说：嗯，对不起，这不适合

sentences.en: the experiment.
sentences.zh: 这项实验。

sentences.en: And rearranged everything, put it back the way it was in the second part of the trial, where
sentences.zh: 接着把一切重新布置，恢复到实验第二部分时的样子，而在那部分里，

sentences.en: people would be perfectly happy to work in these decorated offices.
sentences.zh: 人们本可以高高兴兴地在这些装饰好的办公室里工作。

sentences.en: What they weren't happy with was having someone come in, override their decisions, take
sentences.zh: 他们无法接受的是有人走进来，否决他们的决定，剥夺

sentences.en: away their control, take away their autonomy.
sentences.zh: 他们的控制权，剥夺他们的自主权。

sentences.en: They felt physically sick.
sentences.zh: 他们感到身体不适。

sentences.en: And they hated everything about it.
sentences.zh: 他们讨厌这里的一切。

sentences.en: They hated the work.
sentences.zh: 他们讨厌这项工作。

sentences.en: They hated the company that was hosting the space.
sentences.zh: 他们讨厌提供这个空间的公司。

sentences.en: And they absolutely hated the experimenter.
sentences.zh: 他们极其讨厌那个实验人员。

sentences.en: And after that, I made two vows to myself.
sentences.zh: 在那之后，我对自己发了两个誓。

sentences.en: Number one, if I'm ever a boss, nobody should make me a boss, by the way.
sentences.zh: 第一，如果我有一天当了老板——顺便说一句，没人应该让我当老板。

sentences.en: If I'm ever a boss, I will never impose a clean desk policy.
sentences.zh: 如果我当了老板，我绝不会强制推行整洁办公桌政策。

sentences.en: And number two, me and my wife, we kind of are the boss in our house.
sentences.zh: 第二，我和我妻子，我们在家里算是掌权的人。

sentences.en: And I no longer ask my children to tidy their rooMs.
sentences.zh: 我不再要求我的孩子们整理他们的房间了。

sentences.en: And you know what?
sentences.zh: 你猜怎么着？

sentences.en: We don't argue about it as much.
sentences.zh: 我们为此争吵的次数变少了。

sentences.en: And the rooms are kind of as messy as they ever were.
sentences.zh: 而且房间跟以前一样乱。

sentences.en: It hasn't made any difference to the physical state of the rooMs.
sentences.zh: 它对房间的物理状态没有任何影响。

sentences.en: There's just a little bit more peace.
sentences.zh: 只是多了一点平静。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好了。

sentences.en: So that's a perfect segue to what I want to talk about next.
sentences.zh: 所以这完美地过渡到了我接下来想谈的话题。

sentences.en: Because I actually want to talk about office space and how we organize office spaces.
sentences.zh: 因为我实际上想谈谈办公空间以及我们如何组织办公空间。

sentences.en: And in fact, I have a clip from the cult classic movie, Office Space, which I'm going to play for you.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我有一个邪典经典电影《办公空间》的片段，我要放给你们听。

sentences.en: Hi, Milton.
sentences.zh: 嗨，米尔顿。

sentences.en: What's happening?
sentences.zh: 最近怎么样？

sentences.en: I'm sorry.
sentences.zh: 对不起。

sentences.en: Um, I'm going to have to ask you to go ahead and move your desk again.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我要请你继续把你的办公桌再挪一下。

sentences.en: So if you could go ahead and get it as far back against that wall as possible, that would be great.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你能把它尽量往后靠着那面墙，那就太好了。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: No, because I was that way.
sentences.zh: 不，因为我刚才就是那样放的。

sentences.en: That way we'll have some room for some of these boxes and things we need to put in here.
sentences.zh: 那样我们才会有一些空间来放这些我们需要放进来的箱子和其他东西。

sentences.en: And, uh, oh.
sentences.zh: 还有，呃，哦。

sentences.en: Oh, there it is.
sentences.zh: 哦，在这呢。

sentences.en: Here, let me just go ahead and get that from you.
sentences.zh: 来，让我直接帮你把它拿走。

sentences.en: Great.
sentences.zh: 太好了。

sentences.en: So, if you could just get to that as soon as possible, that would be terrific.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你能尽快把这个处理好，那就太棒了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Thanks a bunch, Milton.
sentences.zh: 多谢了，米尔顿。

sentences.en: Goodbye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Steve, I could set the building on fire.
sentences.zh: 史蒂夫，我可能会把这栋楼给烧了。

sentences.en: So, I take it, Tim, that you're not a fan of fascist office managers.
sentences.zh: 所以，蒂姆，我猜你不是法西斯式办公室经理的粉丝。

sentences.en: Uh,
sentences.zh: 呃，

sentences.en: but you do also tell the story in the book about Steve Jobs at Pixar and some of the ideas he had about how to organize office space to make people more collaborative and some of the ways that might have backfired.
sentences.zh: 但你也在书中讲了关于皮克斯动画工作室的史蒂夫·乔布斯的故事，以及他关于如何组织办公空间以增强人们合作的一些想法，以及这些想法可能带来反效果的一些方式。

sentences.en: Yeah, the Pixar story, I think, is fascinating.
sentences.zh: 对，皮克斯的故事，我觉得非常吸引人。

sentences.en: So, Steve Jobs, majority shareholder at Pixar, had a big hand in designing the Pixar building.
sentences.zh: 所以，皮克斯的大股东史蒂夫·乔布斯，在设计皮克斯大楼时发挥了很大作用。

sentences.en: And one of his big ideas is we are going to make all the bathrooms in this building in the middle of the building.
sentences.zh: 他的一个大胆想法是，我们要把这栋楼里所有的洗手间都设在大楼中央。

sentences.en: We're just going to have two big restrooms, a pair of restrooms in the heart of the building.
sentences.zh: 我们只在大楼的心脏地带设两个大型洗手间，一对洗手间。

sentences.en: And what that will do is everyone will come together, brought together by a shared human need to urinate.
sentences.zh: 这样做的效果是，每个人都会聚到一起，因为人类共同的排泄需求而汇聚在一起。

sentences.en: And there will be serendipitous interactions, and that's going to be great.
sentences.zh: 就会产生意想不到的偶遇互动，那将会非常棒。

sentences.en: And, you know, I'm all in favor of serendipitous interaction.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我完全赞成这种不期而遇的互动。

sentences.en: You know, we silo ourselves off.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们总是把自己孤立起来。

sentences.en: That's a major theme in the book.
sentences.zh: 这是书中的一个主要主题。

sentences.en: Um, but maybe Steve had taken this idea too far.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但史蒂夫可能把这个想法推得太远了。

sentences.en: What's interesting, though, is Steve Jobs had this reputation as being brilliant, but, you know, real control freak's control freak, and just ordering people what to do.
sentences.zh: 不过有趣的是，史蒂夫·乔布斯有着天才的名声，但也确实是个彻头彻尾的控制狂，总是对别人指手画脚。

sentences.en: But there was a rebellion in Pixar, led by pregnant women, who said, I know this sounds like a great idea on paper, Mr. Jobs, but I need to go to the restroom three times an hour.
sentences.zh: 但皮克斯内部发生了一场叛乱，由孕妇们发起，她们说：乔布斯先生，我知道这个想法在纸面上听起来很棒，但我每小时需要去三次洗手间。

sentences.en: And you've just made the restroom ten minutes away from my desk, and do the maths, and it's not going to work.
sentences.zh: 而你刚把洗手间设在离我座位十分钟路程的地方，算算时间，这根本行不通。

sentences.en: And Steve Jobs did an amazing thing.
sentences.zh: 而史蒂夫·乔布斯做了一件了不起的事。

sentences.en: He backed down.
sentences.zh: 他妥协了。

sentences.en: He said, okay, I'm wrong.
sentences.zh: 他说：好吧，我错了。

sentences.en: I will find another way to create serendipitous interactions, and you can have your restrooms all over the Pixar offices, which is where they are.
sentences.zh: 我会找到别的方法来创造机缘巧合的互动，而你的洗手间可以遍布皮克斯办公室的各个角落，本来它们就是这样的。

sentences.en: And reading a recent book about Pixar by Ed Catmull, who is one of the bosses there, it is apparently absolute chaos in there, in a beautiful, beautiful way.
sentences.zh: 读了一本最近出版的关于皮克斯的书，作者是那里的老板之一艾德·卡特姆，里面显然是一片绝对的混乱，但这种混乱美得不可方物。

sentences.en: So the building is just what you would expect from Steve Jobs.
sentences.zh: 所以这座建筑完全符合你对史蒂夫·乔布斯的期待。

sentences.en: It looks gorgeous.
sentences.zh: 它看起来美极了。

sentences.en: It's sort of exposed steel girders and brickwork and wood and all of that.
sentences.zh: 它有点像那种露出的钢梁、砖墙、木材以及所有这些元素。

sentences.en: But the desk space, the Pixar designers build Disney castles and underground, you know, and it looks like the set of Finding Nemo and Toy Story and Wall-E all put into one.
sentences.zh: 但是办公桌区域，皮克斯的设计师们搭建了迪士尼城堡和地下世界，你知道的，它看起来就像《海底总动员》、《玩具总动员》和《机器人总动员》的片场融合在了一起。

sentences.en: It's a great collaborative space that people feel they have control over.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常棒的协作空间，人们觉得他们能够掌控这里。

sentences.en: It looks like a total mess.
sentences.zh: 它看起来一团糟。

sentences.en: In other words, it looks like your children's rooMs.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，它看起来就像你孩子的房间。

sentences.en: Yeah, maybe slightly more creative than my children's rooms, but my children aspire towards the whole Disney castle thing.
sentences.zh: 是的，可能比我孩子的房间稍微更有创意一点，但我孩子向往的是整个迪士尼城堡那一套。

sentences.en: Tim Harford comes from Britain.
sentences.zh: 蒂姆·哈福德来自英国。

sentences.en: We are having this chat in the United States.
sentences.zh: 我们正在美国进行这场交谈。

sentences.en: In both countries, there have been enormous political upheavals recently.
sentences.zh: 在这两个国家，最近都发生了巨大的政治动荡。

sentences.en: When we come back, I'm going to ask Tim about messiness in public life and in democracy.
sentences.zh: 稍后回来，我将向蒂姆询问公众生活和民主中的混乱状态。

sentences.en: Stay with us.
sentences.zh: 请继续收听。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: So with Brexit and the election of Donald Trump, Tim, we've had populist revolutions on both sides of the Atlantic that reject the advice of scientists and economists,
sentences.zh: 蒂姆，随着英国脱欧和唐纳德·特朗普的当选，我们在大西洋两岸都经历了民粹主义革命，它们拒绝科学家和经济学家的建议，

sentences.en: experts in general.
sentences.zh: 以及总体的专家意见。

sentences.en: Democracy, of course, is famously messy.
sentences.zh: 当然，民主素以混乱著称。

sentences.en: Could you remind people why it's such a good thing?
sentences.zh: 你能提醒大家为什么它是一件好事吗？

sentences.en: Yes, I think in both cases, I try to remind myself of Keith Jarrett's unplayable piano, actually.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为在这两种情况下，我实际上都在试图让自己想起基思· Jarrett 那架无法弹奏的钢琴。

sentences.en: To me, the Brexit vote felt like an unplayable piano.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，脱欧公投感觉就像是一架无法弹奏的钢琴。

sentences.en: The expert consensus in the UK was that this was not a very good idea.
sentences.zh: 英国的专家共识是，这不是一个好主意。

sentences.en: The British people disagreed with the experts, and so they voted to leave.
sentences.zh: 英国人民不同意专家的意见，所以他们投票选择离开。

sentences.en: And so I thought to myself, okay, well, this is going to pose all kinds of obstacles and all kinds of difficulties.
sentences.zh: 所以我当时想，好吧，这将会带来各种各样的障碍和各种各样的困难。

sentences.en: In what ways might they actually turn to our advantage?
sentences.zh: 它们在哪些方面实际上可以转化为我们的优势呢？

sentences.en: So not to try to be foolishly optimistic in the face of disappointment, or what was disappointment for a lot of people, but to say, well, there is an opportunity in everything.
sentences.zh: 因此，不是在面对失望时盲目乐观，或者说对许多人来说是失望，而是去说，好吧，任何事情中都蕴含着机遇。

sentences.en: What are the solutions that we look for going forward?
sentences.zh: 我们展望未来时寻找的解决方案是什么？

sentences.en: And I think that's an important thing to bear in mind.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是需要牢记的一点。

sentences.en: Whenever we're faced with an obstacle, it's easy to get frustrated, but we should then say, okay, how is this going to make me stronger?
sentences.zh: 每当我们遇到障碍时，很容易感到沮丧，但我们随后应该说，好吧，这将如何让我变得更强大？

sentences.en: How is this going to make my society stronger?
sentences.zh: 这将如何让我的社会变得更强大？

sentences.en: What are the solutions that are going to come out of disappointment?
sentences.zh: 从失望中将诞生怎样的解决方案？

sentences.en: Donald Trump ran a campaign that many people thought was extremely disordered.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普发起的竞选活动被许多人认为极其无序。

sentences.en: He didn't listen to the experts.
sentences.zh: 他不听取专家的意见。

sentences.en: He went off script all the time.
sentences.zh: 他总是脱离既定稿子。

sentences.en: He said things that people said would be sure to make him lose.
sentences.zh: 他说了一些别人认为肯定会让他输掉的话。

sentences.en: Now, your book came out only a few weeks ago, but clearly, he must have read an early draft.
sentences.zh: 现在，你的书才出版了几周，但显然，他一定读过早期草稿。

sentences.en: I deny leaking the book to Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 我否认将这本书泄露给唐纳德·特朗普。

sentences.en: However, you're absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 不过，你完全说得对。

sentences.en: There is a section in the book about Donald Trump's campaigning style that was written before he won the election, and it was published before he won the election.
sentences.zh: 书中有一个章节专门讲唐纳德·特朗普的竞选风格，这是在他赢得大选之前写的，并且在他赢得大选之前就已经出版了。

sentences.en: And I said he is a master of using chaos to his advantage.
sentences.zh: 我说他是利用混乱为自己谋利的大师。

sentences.en: One of the interesting parallels between Trump's campaign and the Brexit vote in the UK is that the Brexit vote in the UK, there were two different leave campaigns,
sentences.zh: 特朗普的竞选与英国脱欧投票之间的一个有趣相似之处在于，英国脱欧投票中，有两个不同的脱欧阵营，

sentences.en: and they hated each other.
sentences.zh: 而他们互相仇恨。

sentences.en: They were taking legal action against each other.
sentences.zh: 他们互相采取法律行动。

sentences.en: They actively contradicted each other.
sentences.zh: 他们公然互相矛盾。

sentences.en: This may sound familiar.
sentences.zh: 这听起来可能很熟悉。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: You would think that that's a disadvantage.
sentences.zh: 你可能会认为这是一个劣势。

sentences.en: It turns out to be an advantage because they were able to coalesce two different groups of supporters who wanted different things,
sentences.zh: 事实证明这是一个优势，因为他们能够将两拨想要不同东西的支持者联合起来，

sentences.en: and they just tuned into the things they liked to hear.
sentences.zh: 而他们只是关注自己喜欢听的事情。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, the opposition, the remain vote in the UK, the Democrats in the United States, they weren't sure what to criticize because there was no coherence on the other side,
sentences.zh: 与此同时，反对派，英国的留欧派，美国的民主党人，他们不确定该批评什么，因为另一方没有连贯性，

sentences.en: so there was no target to aim at.
sentences.zh: 所以没有可以瞄准的目标。

sentences.en: Trump, by the way, is not the only person to use this.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，特朗普并不是唯一一个使用这种策略的人。

sentences.en: The use of chaos as a weapon works perfectly well in wartime.
sentences.zh: 在战时，将混乱作为武器的策略同样非常有效。

sentences.en: I talk about Erwin Rommel, the great German tank commander.
sentences.zh: 我谈到了埃尔温·隆美尔，这位伟大的德国装甲兵指挥官。

sentences.en: It works in business, Jeff Bezos at Amazon, explicitly targeted, we're going to move fast, we're going to make a mess, we don't understand what's going on,
sentences.zh: 它在商业中也管用，亚马逊的杰夫·贝佐斯明确提出，我们要快速行动，我们要把事情搞砸，我们不知道发生了什么，

sentences.en: but at least Barnes and Noble are more confused than we are.
sentences.zh: 但至少巴诺书店比我们更糊涂。

sentences.en: And as long as Barnes and Noble are more confused than we are, we're doing okay.
sentences.zh: 只要巴诺书店比我们更糊涂，我们就过得还不错。

sentences.en: He was very, very clear about this, and it has proved very effective.
sentences.zh: 他对此非常非常明确，事实证明这非常有效。

sentences.en: I want to talk about another example of messiness in public life, and I want you to watch this video, which describes a very famous speech.
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈公共生活中混乱的另一个例子，我想让你看这段视频，它描述了一场非常著名的演讲。

sentences.en: And I want to ask the question right after it.
sentences.zh: 我想紧接着问一个问题。

sentences.en: We can never be satisfied as long as our children are stripped of their selfhood and robbed of their dignity by signs stating for whites only.
sentences.zh: 只要我们的孩子依然被写着“仅限白人”的标语剥夺自我和尊严，我们就绝不会满足。

sentences.en: We cannot be satisfied as long as a Negro in Mississippi cannot vote, and a Negro in New York believes he has nothing for which to vote.
sentences.zh: 只要密西西比州的黑人无法投票，而纽约州的黑人认为自己无可投之票，我们就不能满足。

sentences.en: So as you can see from that speech, Tim, Martin Luther King is reading from a script, and he has a nice line there, but it's a writerly line.
sentences.zh: 所以从那段演讲中你可以看出，蒂姆，马丁·路德·金是在照着稿子念，他那里有一句不错的台词，但那是一句写出来的台词。

sentences.en: But at a certain point in the speech, he decides to leave the script behind and turn his eyes to the audience, and here's what we see after that.
sentences.zh: 但在演讲的某个时刻，他决定放下讲稿，将目光投向观众，以下是我们在那之后看到的。

sentences.en: I still have a dream.
sentences.zh: 我仍然有一个梦想。

sentences.en: It is a dream deeply rooted in the American dream.
sentences.zh: 这个梦想深深扎根于美国梦之中。

sentences.en: I have a dream.
sentences.zh: 我有一个梦想。

sentences.en: But one day, this nation will rise up and live out the true meaning of its creed.
sentences.zh: 总有一天，这个国家会站起来，活出其信条的真正含义。

sentences.en: We hold these truths to be self-evident, that all men are created equal.
sentences.zh: 我们认为这些真理是不言而喻的，人人生而平等。

sentences.en: Talk about this for a second, because you talk about this speech in the book,
sentences.zh: 请谈谈这个，因为你在书中谈到了这次演讲，

sentences.en: and you talk about this moment when King left his notes behind and essentially stepped off the ledge of what he knew and what he was certain about,
sentences.zh: 你谈到了金放下笔记的那个时刻，他本质上走出了他所知和确定的悬崖边缘，

sentences.en: and just rode the wave of what the crowd was telling him and what he was feeling.
sentences.zh: 顺应着人群告诉他的东西以及他当时的感受顺势而为。

sentences.en: He had prepared that speech meticulously the night before.
sentences.zh: 他前一天晚上精心准备了那篇演讲。

sentences.en: He stayed up very late.
sentences.zh: 他熬夜到很晚。

sentences.en: He was operating under a number of constraints.
sentences.zh: 他在诸多限制下运作。

sentences.en: It was quite a tight time schedule.
sentences.zh: 时间表相当紧凑。

sentences.en: The eyes of the world were on him.
sentences.zh: 全世界的目光都聚焦在他身上。

sentences.en: He knew that.
sentences.zh: 他很清楚这一点。

sentences.en: There were also various political constraints about what was his response going to be to the civil rights legislation.
sentences.zh: 对于他将如何回应民权立法，也存在各种政治限制。

sentences.en: Would he embrace it?
sentences.zh: 他会拥护它吗？

sentences.en: Would he criticize it as not going far enough?
sentences.zh: 他会批评它走得还不够远吗？

sentences.en: Other civil rights leaders were making different claiMs.
sentences.zh: 其他民权领袖提出了不同的诉求。

sentences.en: He had to balance all of those.
sentences.zh: 他必须平衡所有这些因素。

sentences.en: So he took great care.
sentences.zh: 因此他格外小心。

sentences.en: The result was a speech that was well-crafted, but a little bit lifeless.
sentences.zh: 结果是一篇精心雕琢但略显生气的演讲。

sentences.en: And so six or seven minutes into the speech, he looks down at the script, and there's a line there that's terrible.
sentences.zh: 所以在演讲进行到六七分钟时，他低头看了一眼讲稿，那里有一句糟糕的台词。

sentences.en: And it must have been terrible when he wrote it, but he looked and he realized it's not working.
sentences.zh: 当他写下它时一定觉得很糟，但他看了一眼并意识到这行不通。

sentences.en: Now let us go back to our communities as members for the Society for Creative Dissatisfaction.
sentences.zh: 现在让我们作为“创造性不满协会”的成员回到我们的社区中去。

sentences.en: He doesn't say it.
sentences.zh: 他没有说这句话。

sentences.en: He says instead, go back.
sentences.zh: 他转而说道，回去吧。

sentences.en: Go back to Alabama.
sentences.zh: 回到阿拉巴马去。

sentences.en: Go back to Alabama.
sentences.zh: 回到阿拉巴马去。

sentences.en: Go back to South Carolina.
sentences.zh: 回到南卡罗来纳去。

sentences.en: Go back to Georgia.
sentences.zh: 回到佐治亚去。

sentences.en: Go back to Louisiana.
sentences.zh: 回到路易斯安那去。

sentences.en: Go back to the slums and ghettos of our northern cities.
sentences.zh: 回到我们北方城市的贫民窟和黑人聚居区去。

sentences.en: And there's another pause.
sentences.zh: 又是一阵停顿。

sentences.en: And the people behind him on the stage know he's not on the script anymore.
sentences.zh: 台上的其他人知道他已经脱稿了。

sentences.en: And Mahalia Jackson, great gospel singer, yells out to him, because she's heard him talking in church about this dream.
sentences.zh: 伟大的福音歌手玛哈莉亚·杰克逊向他大声呼喊，因为她听过他在教堂里谈论这个梦想。

sentences.en: She yells out, tell him about the dream, Martin.
sentences.zh: 她大喊道，跟他说说那个梦想，马丁。

sentences.en: And then he starts to improvise.
sentences.zh: 然后他开始即兴发挥。

sentences.en: And that is when he touches the crowd.
sentences.zh: 正是在那个时候，他打动了人群。

sentences.en: I want to wrap by asking you a few personal questions.
sentences.zh: 我想问你几个私人问题来作为结束。

sentences.en: I understand that after writing this book, every time you find yourself in a mess and you turn to your wife for comfort, she now reminds you that being in a mess is a good thing.
sentences.zh: 据我了解，在写完这本书后，每当你发现自己陷入混乱并向妻子寻求安慰时，她现在都会提醒你，陷入混乱是一件好事。

sentences.en: Actually, just two days ago, Shankar, I was trying to check into a hotel at Dublin airport at midnight,
sentences.zh: 其实就在两天前，尚卡尔，我试图在午夜时分办理都柏林机场一家酒店的入住，

sentences.en: knowing that I was going to have to get up very early in the morning and fly and then come over to Washington to speak to you.
sentences.zh: 我知道我清晨必须早起乘飞机，然后赶往华盛顿跟你对话。

sentences.en: And I was just desperate to get that little bit of sleep that I would be able to get.
sentences.zh: 我当时极度渴望能获得哪怕一点点我能抓住的睡眠。

sentences.en: And when I showed up at the airport hotel, they didn't have my reservation.
sentences.zh: 当我出现在机场酒店时，他们没有我的预订。

sentences.en: And they were full.
sentences.zh: 而且他们客满了。

sentences.en: So nowhere to sleep.
sentences.zh: 所以没地方睡觉。

sentences.en: And as I toured Dublin in a taxi looking for hotels that were open, I could just hear my wife's voice in my head saying, this is making you smarter, Tim.
sentences.zh: 当我在都柏林坐着出租车寻找开着的酒店时，我脑海里一直回响着我妻子的声音，她说，这会让你变得更聪明，蒂姆。

sentences.en: This is what you say.
sentences.zh: 这就是你说的。

sentences.en: This is making you more creative.
sentences.zh: 这会让你更有创意。

sentences.en: So, you know, I've really sort of created a rod to beat myself with.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我真的是作茧自缚了。

sentences.en: But I think it's important.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这很重要。

sentences.en: Look, sometimes bad news is just bad news.
sentences.zh: 听着，有时坏消息就是坏消息。

sentences.en: Sometimes an obstacle is just an obstacle.
sentences.zh: 有时障碍就是障碍。

sentences.en: And there is no good side to be found.
sentences.zh: 根本找不到好的一面。

sentences.en: But very often, when things go wrong, we need to stop and say, well, what could come out of this?
sentences.zh: 但很多时候，当事情出错时，我们需要停下来想想，嗯，这能带来什么呢？

sentences.en: Brian Eno, a musician who I interviewed for the book, he worked with David Bowie, worked with U2, Coldplay, an amazing producer.
sentences.zh: 布赖恩·伊诺，我为这本书采访过的一位音乐家，他曾与大卫·鲍伊、U2、酷玩乐队合作，是一位了不起的制作人。

sentences.en: He described his creative strategy as a little bit similar to being in an accident.
sentences.zh: 他将自己的创作策略描述为有点类似于遭遇事故。

sentences.en: When you're in an accident, you get that sudden feeling of you're paying attention to everything because there's this tremendous sense of threat.
sentences.zh: 当你遭遇事故时，你会有一种突然的感觉，即你正在关注一切，因为有一种巨大的威胁感。

sentences.en: Well, but that attention, the threat is bad.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但这种注意力，威胁是糟糕的。

sentences.en: The accident is bad.
sentences.zh: 事故是糟糕的。

sentences.en: But the attention is good.
sentences.zh: 但注意力是好的。

sentences.en: And so he puts the musicians he works with in stressful situations.
sentences.zh: 所以他把他合作的音乐家置于压力重重的境地中。

sentences.en: So they feel almost like they've been in an accident.
sentences.zh: 让他们感觉自己几乎遭遇了事故一样。

sentences.en: And suddenly he has their attention.
sentences.zh: 突然间他赢得了他们的注意力。

sentences.en: I think it's worth bearing in mind, even if the accident is a problem, even if the obstacle is a problem, the sudden attention,
sentences.zh: 我认为这值得牢记，即使事故是个问题，即使障碍是个问题，这种突如其来的注意力，

sentences.en: the sudden feeling of being present may lead us to some kind of solution.
sentences.zh: 这种突如其来的临在感可能会引导我们找到某种解决方案。

sentences.en: And that's worth hanging on to.
sentences.zh: 而这值得坚持。

sentences.en: When everything is perfect, when everything is tidy, we're on autopilot.
sentences.zh: 当一切都完美时，当一切都有条不紊时，我们就在自动驾驶。

sentences.en: And we're not necessarily living in the moment.
sentences.zh: 我们不一定活在当下。

sentences.en: We're not necessarily paying attention.
sentences.zh: 我们不一定在集中注意力。

sentences.en: And that's a problem for us.
sentences.zh: 这对我们来说是个问题。

sentences.en: Tim Hartford, thank you for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 蒂姆·哈福德，谢谢你今天加入我。

sentences.en: Thanks, Shankar.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，尚卡尔。
